posts.text: An analysis of tree-ring data from 1,200 fire-scarred trees suggests that the area of dry-conifer forest in New Mexico’s Jemez Mountains could be halved by 2055—a loss caused by mismanagement and wildfires made more destructive by climate change. In PNAS: https://ow.ly/GWrW50ZJsWv

posts.external_title: Insects could face an uphill battle adapting to climate change - British Ecological Society
posts.external_description: Lower oxygen levels and air pressure at higher elevations could pose a barrier to insects moving upslope.

posts.text: Under a warming climate, many species are shifting their range to higher elevations to remain in suitable temperature zones. However, conditions at higher elevations, such as thinner air and less oxygen, pose unique challenges to insects because of their size, lifecycle and way of breathing.

Insects could face an uphill battle adapting to climate change.

A new review of research in @funecology.bsky.social found that lower oxygen levels and air pressure at higher elevations could pose a barrier to some insect species moving upslope to escape climate warming.
